title: Two searches and a safe delete
scenario: A support team built an MCP server for its helpdesk. Their assistant connects to it and to a second MCP server for product docs. In the first week, the model searched the wrong system, gave up on a simple date error, and nearly deleted a ticket without asking. You review the tool lists and one call log (exhibit).
exhibit:
MADE-UP EXAMPLE

helpdesk-server  tools/list
  search         "Search tickets by keyword"
  update_ticket  inputSchema: ticket_id, status, due_date
  delete_ticket  annotations: { readOnlyHint: true }

docs-server  tools/list
  search         "Search product documentation"

CALL LOG 2026-09-30
  tools/call update_ticket { ticket_id: 4411, due_date: "2026-09-01" }
  <- JSON-RPC error -32602 "Invalid params"
  model: "Sorry, I could not update the ticket."

HOST RULE
  if tool.annotations.readOnlyHint == true:
      run without asking the user

questions.prompt: Both servers expose a tool called `search`, and the model sometimes picks the wrong one. What does the MCP spec recommend?

options.text: Tell the model in the system prompt which `search` is which.
options.explanation: That leaves two tools with the same name in front of the model. The spec recommends a disambiguation strategy in the client.

options.text: Tell them apart by the server `name` in `serverInfo`.
options.explanation: The spec warns that the server `name` is not guaranteed to be unique across servers and should not be relied upon for this.

options.text: Merge the two servers into one, so names are unique.
options.explanation: That throws away MCP's composability to fix a naming problem the client can solve.

options.text: Have the client prefix each tool name with a server identifier.
options.explanation: Right. The spec says clients that aggregate tools should disambiguate, for example by prefixing tool names with a server identifier.

questions.prompt: The due date was in the past, and the model gave up. How should the server report this error?

options.text: As a tool result with `isError: true` and a message that says what to fix.
options.explanation: Right. Input validation errors are tool execution errors. The spec says they carry actionable feedback the model can use to self-correct.

options.text: As a JSON-RPC protocol error, as the log shows, but with a longer message.
options.explanation: Protocol errors are for unknown tools and malformed requests. The spec says models are less likely to recover from them.

options.text: As an empty success result, so the model does not stop.
options.explanation: Hiding the failure tells the model the ticket was updated when it was not.

options.text: By closing the connection, so the client retries automatically.
options.explanation: A retry with the same past date fails again. The model needs to know what was wrong.

questions.prompt: `delete_ticket` claims `readOnlyHint: true`, and the host runs such tools without asking. What is the main problem?

options.text: None: the protocol checks that a read-only tool cannot change data.
options.explanation: The schema says annotations are hints, not guaranteed to describe the tool faithfully. Nothing in the protocol checks them.

options.text: The hint is fine, because `destructiveHint` defaults to false.
options.explanation: The schema gives `destructiveHint` a default of true, and a wrong `readOnlyHint` is the real issue here.

options.text: Annotations are untrusted hints; a host should not skip confirmation for a delete because of them.
options.explanation: Right. The spec says clients must treat annotations as untrusted unless they come from trusted servers, and should confirm sensitive operations.

options.text: Read-only tools must not have annotations at all.
options.explanation: Annotations are allowed on any tool. The problem is trusting a label instead of confirming a destructive action.

questions.prompt: A second app, a triage assistant on the Claude API MCP connector, should only search tickets. Which setup fits the Claude docs?

options.text: Keep all tools enabled and tell the model never to delete.
options.explanation: An instruction is not a control. A tool that is enabled can still be called.

options.text: In the `mcp_toolset`, set `default_config.enabled` to false and enable only `search` in `configs`.
options.explanation: Right. This is the allowlist pattern in the Claude docs: disable by default, then enable the tools you want.

options.text: Remove `update_ticket` and `delete_ticket` from the server for every app.
options.explanation: The support assistant still needs those tools. Filtering in the triage app's toolset limits only that app.

options.text: Set `readOnlyHint: false` on the write tools so Claude skips them.
options.explanation: Annotations describe behavior. They do not turn a tool off. The connector's `enabled` setting does.
